links.targetTitle: Safe Harbor pre-authorizes whitehats to seize at-risk funds

title: Sky sets retainable to false, so a rescuer must surrender the entire recovered amount before being paid anything
content:
A.2.11.1.2.2.3.2.5 defines `retainable` as whether "the whitehat hacker may retain the bounty out of the funds recovered or must first return the entire recovered amount to the Asset Recovery Address before receiving payment from the protocol." Sky's value is `false`.

The case for it is control and legal hygiene. Self-payment out of rescued assets means a private actor unilaterally sizing and taking their own fee from funds that may include user deposits, and it forecloses any dispute about whether the amount taken was correct. Requiring full return keeps every disbursement inside governance and keeps the rescuer's conduct cleanly characterizable as custody-and-return.

The cost is that all the trust runs one direction. The rescuer takes the technical and legal risk, then gives up the only leverage they have, and is left with an unsecured expectation against a DAO — payable via Executive Vote, tranched at 1,000,000 USD per month if large, and screened for KYC and sanctions before they qualify at all.

This is the same asymmetry seen throughout the Support Scope's protective instruments: Sky retains discretion over payment while asking counterparties to perform first. Whether it holds depends on reputation, since a single public non-payment would be observed by exactly the population whose cooperation the mechanism needs.
description: The parameter forbids deducting the bounty from rescued funds; the whitehat returns everything to the Asset Recovery Address and then relies on Sky's governance process for payment.
